shared.why: The verdict and the two guardrails — shown for every discipline.

ecommerce.why: How many visits buy, how much they spend, and what each visit earns.

digital_marketing.why: Earned traffic, new buyers, and whether owned messages are read.

performance_marketing.why: What media really earned (D1), what a new customer costs, and ROAS shown beside them to explain why it is not ROI.

digital_growth.why: Whether customers come back, how soon, and whether the first 90 days paid back their acquisition.

agentic_ai.why: How much agent work a person accepts, what it costs, and how often a person corrects it.

automations.why: Whether the workflows run, what a run costs, and whether data arrives intact.

metrics.name: Incremental contribution
metrics.definition: The extra contribution an action or component caused, from the store's own orders.
metrics.formula: holdout: (contribution per assigned test customer − per assigned control customer) × test customers; before/after: contribution in the measurement period − the equal period before. Order contribution = net revenue − product cost − shipping − payment fee − refunds + restocked cost; the discount is never subtracted again
metrics.pdf: T1 Economics — incremental outcome; ROI formula
metrics.note: Store contribution (Growth P&L) is context, never this figure.

metrics.name: Verified avoided cost
metrics.definition: Paid spending that genuinely fell — a cancelled service, a smaller invoice.
metrics.formula: paid cost before − paid cost after, from invoices, with an evidence note; confidence documented
metrics.pdf: T1 cost savings; 06 Economic proof — verified cash saved
metrics.note: Freed hours are never avoided cost.

metrics.name: Net benefit
metrics.definition: What an action earned after everything it cost.
metrics.formula: measured benefit − setup cost − setup hours × hourly rate − operating cost − operating hours × hourly rate
metrics.note: Adopt only when net benefit ≥ the action's hurdle.

metrics.name: ROI (action, full payback)
metrics.definition: Net benefit per euro invested in the action.
metrics.formula: net benefit ÷ (setup cost + setup hours × rate + operating cost + operating hours × rate)
metrics.note: Same formula as the PDF. ROAS and MER are never ROI.

metrics.name: System ROI (continuation)
metrics.definition: Return of the client's running growth system in a month.
metrics.formula: (Σ monthly benefits − Σ monthly operating costs incl. hours × rate) ÷ Σ monthly operating costs, over running components, each benefit_key once
metrics.note: Compared with the client's roi_target; setup is not counted again.

metrics.name: Setup payback
metrics.definition: How much of the setup cost the running components have earned back.
metrics.formula: cumulative net benefit since each component started ÷ total setup cost

metrics.name: Store contribution before marketing
metrics.definition: Growth P&L line: what the month's orders left after product, delivery and payment costs.
metrics.formula: net revenue − refunds − (product cost − restocked cost) − shipping − payment fees
metrics.note: Store health, never an action's benefit; incomplete when a cost is missing.

metrics.name: Store contribution after marketing
metrics.definition: Growth P&L line: store contribution after ad spend.
metrics.formula: contribution before marketing − ad spend
metrics.note: Store health, never an action's benefit.

metrics.name: Contribution margin %
metrics.definition: Share of net revenue, after refunds, left as contribution before marketing.
metrics.formula: contribution before marketing ÷ (net revenue − refunds) × 100
metrics.note: Breach: more than 2 points below the previous three months' average.

metrics.name: Refund rate
metrics.definition: Orders refunded in the period per order placed in it.
metrics.formula: orders refunded in the period ÷ orders placed in the period × 100
metrics.note: Breach: more than 1 point above the previous three months' average.

metrics.name: Sessions
metrics.definition: Visits to the store, by channel when scoped.
metrics.formula: Σ sessions

metrics.name: Orders
metrics.definition: Orders placed.
metrics.formula: count of orders

metrics.name: Net revenue
metrics.definition: Sales after discounts, excluding tax.
metrics.formula: Σ net revenue (refunds are their own P&L line)
metrics.pdf: T1 net sales excluding tax / refunds

metrics.name: Conversion rate
metrics.definition: Orders per session.
metrics.formula: orders ÷ sessions

metrics.name: Average order value
metrics.definition: Net revenue per order.
metrics.formula: net revenue ÷ orders

metrics.name: Contribution per session
metrics.definition: Store contribution per visit — the per-visitor rate most ecommerce plans decide on.
metrics.formula: contribution before marketing ÷ sessions
metrics.pdf: 01 Value & cost KPIs — revenue / visitor (contribution form)
metrics.note: An action's result is still its incremental contribution; this is the store's rate.

metrics.name: Discount rate
metrics.definition: Share of gross sales given away as discounts.
metrics.formula: Σ discounts ÷ (Σ net revenue + Σ discounts)
metrics.note: A lever, read with margin %; discounts are already inside net revenue.

metrics.name: Cost to serve per order
metrics.definition: Delivery and payment cost of an average order.
metrics.formula: (Σ shipping cost + Σ payment fees) ÷ orders
metrics.pdf: 01 Value & cost KPIs — fulfilment / payment / shipping cost per order

metrics.name: Refund value rate
metrics.definition: Share of net revenue given back as refunds.
metrics.formula: Σ refunds recorded in the period ÷ Σ net revenue
metrics.note: Shown beside the refund-rate guardrail.

metrics.name: Units per order
metrics.definition: Items in an average order.
metrics.formula: Σ units ÷ orders

metrics.name: Add-to-cart rate
metrics.definition: Sessions in which something was added to the cart.
metrics.formula: sessions with an add-to-cart ÷ sessions

metrics.name: Checkout completion rate
metrics.definition: Checkouts that became orders.
metrics.formula: orders ÷ sessions that started checkout

metrics.name: Cart abandonment rate
metrics.definition: Carts that never became orders.
metrics.formula: 1 − orders ÷ sessions with an add-to-cart

metrics.name: Mobile conversion rate
metrics.definition: Orders per mobile session.
metrics.formula: mobile orders ÷ mobile sessions

metrics.name: Avoidable return share
metrics.definition: Refunds the store could have prevented.
metrics.formula: refunds with reason damaged, wrong item, not as described or late delivery ÷ all refunds

metrics.name: New customers
metrics.definition: First-time buyers.
metrics.formula: orders with is_new_customer = 1

metrics.name: Message click rate
metrics.definition: Delivered messages that were clicked.
metrics.formula: clicks ÷ delivered
metrics.note: Engagement only. Email-platform-attributed revenue is never used: the holdout is.

metrics.name: Unsubscribe rate
metrics.definition: Delivered messages that made the contact opt out.
metrics.formula: unsubscribes ÷ delivered
metrics.pdf: 02 CRM KPIs — unsubscribe; Channel quality — message fatigue
metrics.note: Watched like a guardrail on message-heavy actions; the two fixed guardrails stay the only ones that flag a breach (decided 2 November).

metrics.name: Message pressure
metrics.definition: Messages each contactable contact received in the month.
metrics.formula: Σ delivered in the month ÷ contactable contacts
metrics.note: Too high drives unsubscribes; too low leaves the list unused.

metrics.name: Delivery rate
metrics.definition: Messages that reached an inbox or a phone.
metrics.formula: delivered ÷ sent
metrics.pdf: 02 CRM KPIs — delivery / bounce; inbox placement

metrics.name: Incremental contribution after media
metrics.definition: What a media change earned: the extra contribution in its channel minus the extra spend — or plus the spend it saved.
metrics.formula: incremental contribution of the orders in the action's channel − change in that channel's ad spend, over the same periods and comparison
metrics.pdf: 04 Measurement — incremental profit; T1 contribution after media
metrics.note: Not measured today: the app's contribution result ignores ad spend and uses the whole store — see D1.

metrics.name: Ad spend
metrics.definition: Paid media cost.
metrics.formula: Σ spend
metrics.note: An input, shown so CPA, CAC and MER can be read.

metrics.name: Cost per order (CPA)
metrics.definition: Media cost of an order.
metrics.formula: ad spend ÷ orders (by channel: channel spend ÷ channel orders)

metrics.name: Customer acquisition cost (CAC)
metrics.definition: Media cost of a new customer.
metrics.formula: ad spend ÷ new customers
metrics.note: Paid CAC; blended or fully loaded CAC would add agency and tool costs.

metrics.name: Cost per paid session
metrics.definition: Media cost of a visit from a paid channel.
metrics.formula: channel spend ÷ channel sessions
metrics.note: Stands in for CPC until clicks exist (E2).

metrics.name: Cost per click (CPC)
metrics.definition: Media cost of a click.
metrics.formula: spend ÷ clicks

metrics.name: Cost per thousand impressions (CPM)
metrics.definition: Media cost of reach.
metrics.formula: spend ÷ impressions × 1,000

metrics.name: Click-through rate (CTR)
metrics.definition: Impressions that were clicked.
metrics.formula: clicks ÷ impressions
metrics.note: A creative and feed diagnostic; never a result.

metrics.name: ROAS
metrics.definition: Store revenue per euro of channel spend.
metrics.formula: channel net revenue (store orders) ÷ channel spend
metrics.note: Never ROI (spec §9: the promotion with ROAS 3.0 had ROI −0.17).

metrics.name: Break-even ROAS
metrics.definition: The ROAS at which a channel's orders only just pay for their own media.
metrics.formula: 1 ÷ contribution margin before marketing (as a ratio)
metrics.pdf: T1 Decision economics — break-even CAC / ROAS
metrics.note: Read beside ROAS: Luna 2.86, Brote 1.67, Roble 4.00 at their profile margins.

metrics.name: Marketing efficiency ratio (MER)
metrics.definition: Store revenue per euro of total ad spend.
metrics.formula: net revenue ÷ total ad spend (cost scope: ad spend only)
metrics.pdf: 04 Optimisation — MER with defined cost scope
metrics.note: MER is not ROI.

metrics.name: New-customer share
metrics.definition: Share of orders from first-time buyers.
metrics.formula: new-customer orders ÷ orders (by channel when scoped)
metrics.pdf: 04 Optimisation — new vs existing customer mix
metrics.note: Plan 31 warns against chasing it: prospecting spend that buys back existing customers is the waste to find.

metrics.name: Platform overcount
metrics.definition: How far the ad platform's purchase count exceeds the store's own orders from that channel.
metrics.formula: platform-reported purchases ÷ store orders from the channel
metrics.pdf: 04 Measurement — attribution model / window, cross-channel overlap
metrics.note: Shows on screen why platform-attributed revenue is never a result.

metrics.name: Tracking capture rate
metrics.definition: Store orders that the analytics purchase tag recorded.
metrics.formula: tagged purchases ÷ store orders
metrics.pdf: T2 Reliability — order reconciliation, event deduplication
metrics.note: Plan 25's acceptance criterion is capture ≥ 98%.

metrics.name: Repeat-purchase rate
metrics.definition: Customers who bought more than once recently.
metrics.formula: customers with two or more orders in the trailing 90 days ÷ customers with one or more

metrics.name: Second-order rate within 90 days
metrics.definition: First-time customers who came back within 90 days.
metrics.formula: first-time customers of a month who order again within 90 days ÷ first-time customers of that month
metrics.pdf: 03 Cohorts — new / returning; Growth detail — purchase frequency
metrics.note: A cohort needs 90 days after its month, so the latest three cohorts show as incomplete.

metrics.name: Orders per customer (180 days)
metrics.definition: How often a customer buys.
metrics.formula: orders ÷ distinct customers over the trailing 180 days

metrics.name: Days to second order
metrics.definition: How long a returning customer took to buy again.
metrics.formula: median days between first and second order, for customers with a second order
metrics.pdf: 03 Growth detail — interpurchase time, time to first value

metrics.name: Reactivation rate
metrics.definition: Lapsed customers who bought again.
metrics.formula: lapsed customers who order in the month ÷ customers lapsed at its start; lapsed = no order for 180 days (occasional stores) or 60 days (monthly stores)
metrics.note: Not used for rare-purchase stores such as Roble.

metrics.name: Cohort contribution at 90 days
metrics.definition: What a new customer has actually earned the store in their first 90 days.
metrics.formula: contribution of a first-time customer's orders in the 90 days from the first order, averaged over the cohort
metrics.pdf: 03 Cohorts — cohort revenue, LTV; T1 revenue- vs contribution-LTV
metrics.note: Realised, never forecast: LTV forecasting stays out of scope (spec §13).

metrics.name: 90-day contribution to CAC
metrics.definition: Whether a new customer's first 90 days paid back what it cost to acquire them.
metrics.formula: cohort contribution at 90 days ÷ CAC of the cohort month
metrics.pdf: T1 Decision economics — contribution-LTV:CAC, CAC payback
metrics.note: Above 1.0, the first 90 days covered paid acquisition.

metrics.name: Output acceptance rate
metrics.definition: Agent outputs a person accepted without a substantive correction.
metrics.formula: outputs accepted ÷ outputs reviewed
metrics.pdf: 05 Agent KPIs — task success, human acceptance / override

metrics.name: Cost per accepted output
metrics.definition: What one usable piece of agent work costs, people included.
metrics.formula: (operating cost + operating hours × hourly rate) ÷ outputs accepted
metrics.note: Plan 60's decision metric.

metrics.name: AI cost per output
metrics.definition: Model and API cost of one output.
metrics.formula: AI cost ÷ outputs

metrics.name: Report correction rate
metrics.definition: Sent client reports a reviewer had to correct substantively.
metrics.formula: sent reports with was_corrected = 1 ÷ sent reports

metrics.name: Report rejection rate
metrics.definition: Report drafts a reviewer rejected.
metrics.formula: rejected drafts ÷ reviewed drafts

metrics.name: Cost per report draft
metrics.definition: Model cost of one report draft.
metrics.formula: Σ generation cost ÷ drafts

metrics.name: Run failure rate
metrics.definition: Runs that failed.
metrics.formula: failed runs ÷ runs
metrics.note: Runs and failed runs are already shown as counts.

metrics.name: Cost per run
metrics.definition: What one run costs, people included.
metrics.formula: (operating cost + operating hours × hourly rate) ÷ runs

metrics.name: Exception rate
metrics.definition: Runs a person had to finish by hand.
metrics.formula: exceptions ÷ runs

metrics.name: Hours freed (capacity)
metrics.definition: Staff hours a component freed in the month.
metrics.formula: as recorded on the component month
metrics.note: Capacity, never money (spec §4) — see 'Where the PDF and the app differ'.

metrics.name: Intake quality
metrics.definition: Share of received shop-data batches that were accepted.
metrics.formula: accepted ÷ received shop-data batches

metrics.name: Duplicate delivery rate
metrics.definition: Events delivered more than once.
metrics.formula: duplicate events ÷ received events
metrics.note: A duplicate already changes nothing (external_id); this counts how often it happens.

metrics.name: Orders with a missing cost
metrics.definition: Orders whose product, shipping or payment cost did not arrive.
metrics.formula: count of orders with any cost missing
metrics.note: Makes the dependent Growth P&L lines incomplete, never zero.

metrics.name: Below-target alerts
metrics.definition: Alerts the below-target automation raised in the month.
metrics.formula: accepted alert events

scorecards.question: Does the store turn its visits into profitable orders?
scorecards.comparison: holdout per visitor or customer where a group can be assigned; otherwise before/after
scorecards.store_fit: All three stores. Roble's few orders (about 36 a week at 0.6%) need a longer window than Luna's or Brote's before any result means anything.

scorecards.question: Does the store earn demand and keep its customers buying, without paying for every visit?
scorecards.comparison: holdout per assigned contact for CRM; before/after on the organic channel for SEO and content (observational)
scorecards.store_fit: CRM fits Brote (monthly) and Luna (occasional); for Roble (rare purchases) the useful levers are search and content. Owned channels have no media cost: their cost is the action's own setup and hours.

scorecards.question: Does each euro of media buy contribution the store would not have had anyway?
scorecards.comparison: before/after on the action's channel; a matched-region holdout when the plan allows it (plan 36)
scorecards.store_fit: All three stores buy media (8–15% of revenue). Until D1 is decided, the result is measured as plain incremental contribution.

scorecards.question: Do first-time buyers come back, and do the stages after the first order grow?
scorecards.comparison: holdout per customer, over the plan's horizon (30–180 days)
scorecards.store_fit: Repeat and reactivation fit Luna (occasional) and Brote (monthly). For Roble (rare purchases) growth means new customers and referral, not repeat.

scorecards.question: Does the agent produce accepted work for less than it costs, with a person reviewing every output?
scorecards.comparison: invoice for saved paid work (documented); holdout for shopper-facing assistants (plans 54, 55)
scorecards.store_fit: Any store. Agents never calculate ROI or forecast (spec §4); freed hours are capacity.

scorecards.question: Does the workflow run reliably, and does it save paid cost or win contribution?
scorecards.comparison: invoice for saved paid work; a kept holdout for customer-facing flows (plan 65)
scorecards.store_fit: Any store; cart recovery needs carts to recover, so it suits Luna and Brote more than Roble.

data_extensions.name: Funnel steps and device
data_extensions.plain: What shoppers did on the site before buying — viewed a product, added to the cart, started checkout — and whether they were on a phone or a computer; plus how many purchases the analytics tag actually recorded.
adds: sessions.device (mobile or desktop), part of the row's key: client · date · channel · device
sessions.product_views, add_to_carts, checkouts_started — sessions that reached each step
sessions.tracked_purchases — purchases the analytics tag recorded

data_extensions.name: Ad delivery and platform-reported purchases
data_extensions.plain: How many people saw and clicked each channel's ads, and how many purchases the ad platform claims — always more than the store really received from it.
adds: ad_spend.platform_purchases, platform_revenue_eur — what the ad platform claims

data_extensions.name: Message sends (email and SMS)
data_extensions.plain: The emails and SMS each store sent — campaigns and automatic flows such as cart recovery — with how many were delivered, clicked and led to an unsubscribe.
adds: new table messages_daily: client · date · channel (email or sms) · stream (a campaign or flow name) · action_id (nullable) · sent · delivered · clicks · unsubscribes · contactable (contacts who could receive the stream that day)

data_extensions.name: Units per order
data_extensions.plain: How many items each order contains, so bundles and cross-selling can be judged.

data_extensions.name: Refund reasons
data_extensions.plain: Why each refund happened — damaged, wrong item, not as described, late, or the customer changed their mind — so preventable returns can be told apart.
adds: refunds.reason CHECK in (damaged, wrong_item, not_as_described, late_delivery, changed_mind); all but changed_mind count as avoidable

data_extensions.name: Agent and automation output counts
data_extensions.plain: For each AI agent and automation, how much work it produced each month, how much of it a person accepted, how often a person had to step in, and what the AI cost.
adds: component_months.outputs, outputs_accepted, exceptions, ai_cost_eur (nullable; automation and agent components only)

params.Luna analytics agent (plan 50): 4 outputs a month (weekly report), 3–4 accepted, no exceptions; AI cost = Σ generation cost of the month's report drafts
params.Luna cart-recovery flow (plan 65): 30–31 runs a month (daily); outputs = messages sent (E3); 0–3 exceptions; no AI cost
